Dialog.Dxvk.WarningContent:
⚠ ADVANCED FEATURE — USE AT YOUR OWN RISK

DXVK is an unofficial DirectX-to-Vulkan translation layer.
No support will be provided if a game is not compatible.

WHO SHOULD USE THIS:
• Primarily benefits older DX8/DX9 games (e.g. FFXIV, Morrowind)
• Enables ReShade compute shaders on games that don't support them natively
• Can reduce CPU-bound stuttering in older titles

IMPORTANT WARNINGS:
• Anti-cheat games may ban players using DXVK
• Game overlays (Steam, NVIDIA, RTSS) may conflict or stop working
• Exclusive fullscreen is blocked — use borderless windowed
• First launch will be slow due to shader compilation (improves on subsequent runs)
• Some games may crash or have graphical glitches with DXVK

Do you want to continue?
Dialog.DxvkInfo.Content:
DXVK translates DirectX 8/9/10/11 API calls into Vulkan.

Benefits:
• Enables ReShade compute shaders on older DX games
• May improve performance and reduce shader stutter
• Enables HDR output via dxvk.conf
• Borderless fullscreen recommended over exclusive fullscreen

⚠ Anti-cheat games may ban players using DXVK.
⚠ Game overlays (Steam, NVIDIA, RTSS) may conflict.

Dialog.FullRefresh.Content:
This will clear all caches and re-scan everything from scratch:

• Re-detects all games from every storefront
• Re-scans DLSS/Streamline DLL paths
• Re-detects graphics APIs and engine types
• Rebuilds shader and addon deployment state

Try a normal Refresh first — it handles most issues without the full rescan. Use Full Refresh as a last resort if games are missing, paths have changed, DLSS has been added to a game, or the DLSS section is missing from a game card.

The next couple of restarts may take a few seconds longer while caches are rebuilt.

Do not close RHI while the refresh is in progress — closing early will result in a missing library and the scan will need to be repeated.

Faq.Body.AddingGamesManually: If a game isn't detected, click the green + next to the search box and choose its .exe, or drag the .exe onto the RHI window. RHI adds it to your library and detects its engine.
Faq.Body.ChooseShaders:
Click 'Shaders/Addons' in the toolbar, then 'Global Shaders'. Lilium's HDR shaders are selected by default. Your selection is deployed to every game with ReShade.

Expand a pack to pick individual shaders, or search for one. Use the Profiles panel to save named selections, and Export to copy one as a zip you can paste into Discord.
Faq.Body.DlssStreamline:
Games with DLSS or Streamline files have a DLSS / Streamline section. Pick a version for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, Frame Generation, Neural Rendering or Streamline, and RHI swaps the file. Originals are backed up: choose 'Default' or click Restore DLSS/SL to put them back.

You can also set presets and render scale per game. These are written to the NVIDIA driver, so you don't need NVIDIA Profile Inspector.
Faq.Body.DofFix: DOF Fix backports a depth-of-field fix from Unreal Engine 5.7 to games on UE 5.0–5.6. When a game supports it, it appears under Recommended in the Components section. Install it alongside RenoDX for the best result.
Faq.Body.FrameLimiters: ReLimiter and Display Commander are ReShade addons that limit frame rate precisely, which is ideal for VRR displays. Install one of them (not both) from the Components section. ReLimiter is recommended. Set your target FPS in Settings → Components, per game in the ReLimiter ⚙, or in-game.
Faq.Body.FullRefresh: If games are missing, a game has moved, or DLSS files were added or removed, use 'Full refresh' in Settings → Tools & Maintenance to rescan everything from scratch.
Faq.Body.InstallReShade: ReShade is needed for RenoDX, Luma, frame limiters and DOF Fix. Click 'Install ReShade' in the Components section. RHI picks the right file name for the game's graphics API and installs the version with addon support.
Faq.Body.Luma:
Luma is a mod framework by Pumbo. Depending on the game, a Luma mod may add HDR, DLSS, DLAA or rendering fixes. Check the Info button to see what each mod offers.

• Named mods: for supported games, shown on the Luma row. Mods only on Nexus Mods open their Nexus page.
• Generic Luma: for DX11 Unreal Engine games. RHI applies the Engine.ini tweaks and launch arguments listed on the Luma wiki.

Generic Luma can be used alongside RenoDX. Named Luma mods normally replace RenoDX.
Faq.Body.NvidiaDriverSettings: The Driver Settings section changes the game's NVIDIA profile directly. It needs Admin Mode (Settings → General → Admin Mode).
Faq.Body.OptiScaler:
OptiScaler lets a game's DLSS, FSR or XeSS inputs drive a different upscaler (FSR, XeSS, DLSS), and can add or replace frame generation on any GPU. It's in the Extras section.

Before installing, set your GPU type (and DLSS inputs for AMD/Intel) in Settings → Components → OptiScaler. Then choose a variant in the OptiScaler ⚙:
• Stable: official release.
• Nightly: latest build, or pin a specific build.
• DLSS NR and F5 DLSSNR: forks with DLSS Neural Rendering.

The ⚙ also sets the upscaler, frame generation, Reflex, DLSS presets, render scale, Engine.ini fixes and Neural Rendering options, and saves presets you can apply to other games.
Faq.Body.RenoDX:
RenoDX mods give games true HDR output. The RenoDX HDR row shows what's available for the game:

• Named mods: game-specific HDR mods made by the community.
• UE-Extended: for Unreal Engine games without a named mod.
• Generic Unity: for Unity games without a named mod.

A ✓ next to the installed mod means it's complete; a hammer means it's still in progress. Click 'Available Mods' in the toolbar to see every game with a RenoDX, Luma or Ultra+ mod.
Faq.Body.SelectGame:
Your games are listed on the left. Click a game to open its detail panel. Use the search box and the filter chips (All Games, Installed, Favourites, Unreal, Unity, RenoDX, Luma…) to find games.

The detail panel is split into sections: Components, Game Overrides, Neural Rendering, DLSS / Streamline, Driver Settings, Management and Extras. Click a section heading to collapse it, or drag its ≡ handle to reorder.
Faq.Body.Settings: Click 'Settings' in the toolbar for options that apply to all games:
Faq.Body.SystemTray: RHI can keep running in the system tray when you close the window. Right-click the tray icon to launch recent games without opening RHI.
Faq.Body.UpdatingEverything: Click 'Update All' in the toolbar to update ReShade, RenoDX, ReLimiter, Display Commander, OptiScaler, RE Framework, DXVK, Luma and DOF Fix across all your games.
Faq.Body.VulkanGames: Vulkan games (shown with a VLK badge) use a global ReShade layer installed to C:\ProgramData\ReShade. This needs administrator rights, so RHI asks for permission the first time.
Faq.Body.WelcomeToRhi: RHI finds the games on your PC and installs, updates and removes HDR mods, ReShade, shaders, frame limiters, DLSS files and more, and manages your NVIDIA driver settings, all from one place. Here's how to get started.

Faq.Tip.AddingGamesManually:
Wrong folder? Use Management → Change install folder.
Manually added games can be removed with Management → Reset / Remove game.
Faq.Tip.ChooseShaders:
Per-game shaders: Game Overrides → Shaders → Select.
Your own shaders: click Open Custom Folder in the picker's Profiles panel and put them there. They appear under Custom Shaders.
Global Addons, in the same toolbar menu, manages ReShade addons for all games.
Faq.Tip.DlssStreamline:
NVIDIA Override in the version list tells the driver to use its newest DLSS file instead.
Set your preferred versions and presets once in Settings → DLSS / Streamline → Configure Defaults, then use Quick Apply on any game, or Batch Deploy for many games at once.
DLSS section missing? Use Full refresh in Settings → Tools & Maintenance.
Faq.Tip.DofFix:
DOF Fix only appears on 64-bit UE 5.0–5.6 games.
If a game's engine badge just says 'Unreal Engine', click the badge to mark it as Unreal Engine 5.
Faq.Tip.FrameLimiters:
Installing either limiter turns off the NVIDIA driver frame limit for that game.
VRR cap presets by refresh rate (a little below max keeps VRR active):
• 60Hz → 59 FPS
• 120Hz → 116 FPS
• 144Hz → 138 FPS
• 165Hz → 157 FPS
• 240Hz → 224 FPS
• 360Hz → 324 FPS
These values are pre-configured in RHI's FPS dropdowns.
Faq.Tip.FullRefresh:
Downloads or update checks failing? Add a GitHub token (Settings → Accounts & Data).
To report a problem, click Copy logs in Settings → Tools & Maintenance and/or Copy Report in the game's Management section, then paste it into Discord.
Faq.Tip.InstallReShade:
Change the ReShade version per game in Game Overrides → ReShade Channel: Stable, Nightly, Custom (your own DLL), No Addons or Legacy.
The ReShade ⚙ deploys reshade.ini or ReShadePreset.ini, sets per-game hotkeys, and can stop RHI changing this game's reshade.ini.
Drag a ReShade preset (.ini) onto RHI to install it, along with the shaders it needs.
Faq.Tip.Luma:
Luma needs ReShade. The install button shows 'ReShade required' until it's installed.
The Luma ⚙ (Unreal games) has HDR on First Boot and TAA settings.
Launch arguments such as -dx11 are added on install and removed on uninstall. They only apply when you launch the game through RHI.
DX9 Luma mods get dgVoodoo2 installed automatically.
Faq.Tip.NvidiaDriverSettings: Global defaults (shader cache, G-Sync, FPS limit, VSync, Power Mode, ReBAR) and profile backup/restore are in Settings → Driver Settings. Digital Vibrance is in Settings → Display & HDR.
Faq.Tip.OptiScaler:
OptiScaler and ReShade can run together. If a game crashes with both, give ReShade a different name in Game Overrides → DLL naming overrides.
'Replace with a fresh copy...' in the ⚙ resets the game's OptiScaler.ini from your template.
Faq.Tip.RenoDX:
The RenoDX ⚙ has per-game peak brightness, UE-Extended and Engine.ini HDR options, compatibility settings, and preset export/import.
No mod for your game? Turn on RTX HDR (NVIDIA) or Auto HDR (Windows 11, any GPU) from the same ⚙. Either one replaces RenoDX for that game.
Got an .addon64 from the RenoDX Discord? Drag it onto RHI and pick the game.
Faq.Tip.SelectGame:
Double-click a game to launch it. Right-click a game to open its folder, favourite or hide it, or create a desktop shortcut.
The HDR and RES buttons next to Launch turn Windows HDR on and switch resolution while the game is running.
Type a search, then click the + that appears to save it as a filter chip.
Faq.Tip.SystemTray:
Turn on Close to Tray, Recent Games and Start with Windows in Settings → General → Windows.
Recent Games also appear in the taskbar jump list.
While running, RHI checks for updates every 4 hours.
Faq.Tip.UpdatingEverything:
Games with updates show a green dot in the sidebar.
Choose what Update All includes in Settings → General → Components to check, or per game in Game Overrides → Update Inclusion.
Turn on Automatic updates in Settings → General to install updates in the background.
The Updates button at the bottom right shows everything that has been updated.
Faq.Tip.VulkanGames:
All Vulkan games share the same ReShade, so changing the ReShade channel on one changes it for all.
RenoDX addons and shaders are still installed to each game's own folder.
Games that support both DirectX and Vulkan: choose one in Game Overrides → Graphics API.

Info.DisplayCommander: Display Commander is a frame limiter that works alongside ReShade to reduce input lag and improve frame pacing.
Info.Luma: Luma is an alternative HDR mod framework that provides native HDR output for supported games, bypassing the need for ReShade-based injection.
Info.OptiScaler: OptiScaler is an upscaling compatibility layer that enables FSR, XeSS, or DLSS across different GPU vendors, allowing you to use any upscaler regardless of your hardware.
Info.ReFramework: RE Framework is a modding framework for RE Engine games. It enables ReShade injection and other mods by hooking into the game's rendering pipeline.
Info.ReLimiter: ReLimiter is a frame limiter that works alongside ReShade to reduce input lag and improve frame pacing in games.
Info.ReShade: ReShade is a post-processing injector that adds visual effects to games. It is required by RenoDX to apply HDR tone mapping and color grading.
Info.RenoDX: RenoDX is an HDR mod framework that upgrades SDR games to HDR using ReShade. It provides per-game tone mapping and color space conversion.
Info.UeExtended: This game is set to use UE-Extended. It is automatically configured to use native HDR and an Engine.ini will be automatically deployed upon installation. If there is an ingame HDR option then enable that too.

Settings.Dldsr.Info.Description:
DLDSR (Deep Learning Dynamic Super Resolution) renders games at higher resolutions and downscales with AI for sharper image quality. This feature lets you switch DLDSR presets without opening NVIDIA Control Panel.

DLDSR uses a Lanczos algorithm — less jaggies, more stable, but can look slightly painterly. Standard DSR uses a Gaussian filter — more natural but with more aliasing. DLDSR is generally sharper than DSR at equivalent settings.

Recommended factors: DLDSR 2.25x offers the best balance of quality and performance. DSR 4.00x uses significantly more VRAM. DLDSR 1.78x is the most VRAM-friendly option.
Settings.Dldsr.Info.SetupSteps:
1. Open NVIDIA Control Panel → Manage 3D Settings → Global Settings
2. Find "DSR - Factors" and enable the DLDSR factors you want (e.g. 1.78x DL, 2.25x DL)
3. Click Apply and wait for the ~15 second display blackout
4. Come back here and click "Capture Current" to save this state
5. Repeat steps 2-4 for each DLDSR configuration you want to save (e.g. "Off", "2.25x only", "1.78x + 2.25x")
Settings.Dldsr.Info.SmoothnessDescriptio:
Controls the sharpening/smoothing applied during downscale. 100 = no sharpening (pure Lanczos downscale). Lower values add sharpening — the image gets progressively sharper as you reduce it.

Recommended DLDSR smoothness values (from r/MotionClarity):
  • 100 — No sharpening
  • 80 — Sharp without artifacts
  • 75 — Clear
  • 65 — Clearer
  • 55-65 — Similar clarity to DSR 4.00x at 0% (recommended range)
  • 45 — As sharp as DSR 4.00x everywhere

Note: DLDSR uses a Lanczos algorithm — it is naturally much sharper than standard DSR (Gaussian), so it requires higher smoothness values for a comparable look.

Changing smoothness causes the same ~15 second display blackout as applying a full state. Tip: set smoothness first, then click Apply — both will apply together in a single restart.

Setup.Description:
RHI can manage ReShade across all your games automatically. Here's what that includes:

  - Installs and updates ReShade for each game with one click
  - Keeps the correct DLL name per game based on what the game needs
  - Manages shader packs globally - install once, deployed to every game automatically
  - Backs up any shaders already in your game folders before taking over
  - Keeps ReShade in sync when you install RenoDX, OptiScaler, or other components

If you already have a custom ReShade setup - specific shader collections, hand-tuned configs, or a version you prefer - choose "I'll manage it myself" and RHI will leave ReShade completely alone.

Extras.Rtx40Mfg.ReShadeWarning.Content:
ReShade is installed in this game. Universal MFG Unlocker's XeSS frame generation ("XeMFG standalone" in its menu) doesn't start while ReShade is loaded: the mod's menu shows "Waiting menu_factory_not_dxgi". This happens whether ReShade is installed as a DLL or as an ASI.

DLSS multi frame generation works as normal. To use XeMFG with ReShade, install OptiScaler (nightly, F5 or DLSS NR) and set FG Output to XeFG in OptiScaler's settings; RHI then installs the mod as an OptiScaler plugin.

Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.Intro: Press Backspace in-game to open the Universal MFG Unlocker menu. It offers these modes:
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.ModeFollowGame: • Follow game: uses the game's own MFG setting
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.ModeFixed: • Fixed 2x to 6x: forces a specific multiplier
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.ModeDynamic: • Dynamic: targets the display refresh rate or a custom FPS value
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.PresetNote: If frames freeze above 2x, set the Frame Generation preset to B in this game's DLSS / Streamline section.
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.OsIntro: OptiScaler loads the mod as a plugin, as its author recommends. Frame generation is chosen in OptiScaler, not here: open OptiScaler's ⚙ and set FG Output to DLSSG for DLSS multi frame generation, or XeFG for XeMFG. OptiScaler's default (Auto) runs no frame generation.
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.OsNote: The mod's own menu still opens beside OptiScaler's for the DLSS presets and DLSS 5. If OptiScaler is removed, RHI moves the mod back next to the game's exe.
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.XessViaOs: Through OptiScaler, XeMFG is OptiScaler's FG Output set to XeFG. It uses the XeSS files OptiScaler installs, so nothing else is needed.
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.XessIntro: The mod can also use Intel's XeSS frame generation, 2x to 6x on any GPU (experimental). Tick "XeMFG standalone" in the in-game menu and restart the game. It needs Intel's libxess_fg.dll and libxell.dll in an RTXMFG-XeSS folder next to the mod; RHI installs them with the mod.
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.XessMissing: XeSS files: missing. Reinstall the mod to add them.
Extras.Rtx40Mfg.Settings.ReShadeDxgiWarn: ReShade is installed as dxgi.dll in this game. With XeMFG at 5x and 6x, some generated frames may not reach the screen. If that happens, give ReShade a different DLL name in Game Overrides › DLL naming overrides.
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.Title: 20/30 FG Unlock Settings
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.Intro: These settings are saved in the game's dlssg_sm86.ini. Exit the game completely and start it again for changes to apply. Needs NVIDIA driver R580 or newer; on older drivers the mod turns itself off.
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.NotInstalled: Install 20/30 FG Unlock on this game to change these settings.
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.Saved: Saved {0}. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.FrameGeneratio: Off leaves the game's own DLSS Frame Generation untouched (no FG on RTX 20/30) without uninstalling.
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.Engine.Label: Engine
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.Engine.Help: DLSS uses NVIDIA's frame generation model. XeSS uses Intel's model: up to 4X, and it doesn't work with HDR (16-bit) output.
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.MaxFrames.Help: The highest multiplier the game can offer. The game's own menu can still pick a lower one. 6X has to be chosen here.
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.XessMaxFrames: XeSS goes up to 4X. Switch Engine to DLSS for 5X or 6X.
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.Preset.Label: Preset
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.Preset.Help: A is the default. B cleans up the HUD in generated frames, but only works if the game provides the extra images (most don't). C is FG Lite: much cheaper to run, slightly lower quality.
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.SpeedTier.Help: How far the image may differ from NVIDIA's official output. Exact tiers match it bit for bit; Fast and Fastest are a few percent quicker with tiny differences.
Extras.Dlssg2030.Settings.SuperResolutio: RTX 20/30 only. Pins DLSS preset M or L. INT8 uses the mod's faster kernels: quicker in Performance and Ultra Performance, slower than the game's default in Quality, Balanced and DLAA. No effect while Ray Reconstruction is on.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Engine.Label: Engine
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Engine.Help: Game keeps the game's own frame generation. XeFG replaces the game's DLSS frame generation with Intel XeSS frame generation. DLSS-FG replaces a game's own Intel frame generation with DLSS frame generation. None of them adds frame generation to a game that has none. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Mode.Label: Mode
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Mode.Help: Game decides: the game (or NVIDIA Profile Inspector) chooses the multiplier. Fixed: the multiplier next to it. Dynamic: frame generation adapts toward a target frame rate (the monitor's refresh rate by default).
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Multiplier.Hel: Used in Fixed mode. 5x and 6x are experimental. On an 8 GB card, 2x or 3x is the safer starting point.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.DLSSFGpreset.H: Game: no override. A and B use normal frame generation; C uses the faster Lite mode (with some image-quality trade-offs) and needs DLSS FG 310.9.16. B needs the game's HUD-less inputs. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Flipmeteringby: Streamline paces the generated frames itself instead of NVIDIA's flip metering. Try it when 3x or 4x looks choppy while 2x is smooth. Restart the game to apply.
1 to 1000 FPS, or 0 for no RTX Encore limit. Applied through Reflex, or through XeLL with XeFG (needs a restart then). Generated frames may count toward the limit. Press Enter or click away to save.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.DynamictargetF: Used in Dynamic mode: the frame rate frame generation adapts toward. 0 follows the refresh rate of the monitor showing the game. Press Enter or click away to save.
Lets Dynamic mode go up to 5x and 6x (needs plenty of VRAM). Off: Dynamic stays at 4x or less.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.NVIDIATensorCo: Runs XeFG on NVIDIA Tensor Cores. RTX 30, 40 and 50 on NVIDIA driver 621.01 or the 621.12 hotfix; only the RTX 4090 has been tested in games. If it can't be used, standard XeFG runs instead.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Variablepacing: Paces XeFG above 2x using the game's real frame timing. Off can make multipliers above 2x unavailable. Restart the game to apply.
Interpolate: the HUD is generated along with the scene. Game layers: uses the game's separate HUD-less and UI images, when the game provides them. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.UIalpha.Label: UI alpha
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.UIalpha.Help: How the game's UI layer stores transparency, for Game layers. Leave Unknown unless you know it: Unknown never guesses and doesn't use UI layers. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Highmultiplier: Keeps generated frames clean from 3x to 6x. Leave on. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Frameprotectio: Protects generated frames against tearing on thin geometry (fences, wires, foliage) and ghosting in moving shadows. No effect with the Lite preset. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Fastframegener: Lowers the GPU cost of each generated frame, with the same image. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Protectiontuni: Refined (default) or Classic. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.AutoUIrecompos: Turns DLSS FG's UI recomposition on when the game provides HUD-less images, even if the game doesn't ask for it. Off follows the game. Turn it off in No Man's Sky (duplicated generated frames).
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.UIassist.Label: UI assist
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.UIassist.Help: DirectX 12: captures the HUD-less scene and builds the UI layer itself when the game doesn't provide them.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.ForceUIrecompo: Asks DLSS FG to recompose the HUD separately even when the game doesn't request it.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Customrendersc: Render scale in percent (50 to 100) when DLSS render scale is Custom. Press Enter or click away to save.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.DLSSrenderscal: Forces the DLSS render resolution. Game: no override. The game must already use DLSS.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Upscaler.Label: Upscaler
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Upscaler.Help: Game keeps the game's DLSS Super Resolution. XeSS replaces compatible DLSS Super Resolution with Intel XeSS. Applies live in DirectX; Vulkan needs XeSS set before the game starts.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.XeSSonTensorCo: Runs XeSS Super Resolution on NVIDIA Tensor Cores (RTX 30, 40 and 50, DirectX 12, driver 621.01 or 621.12; tested on the RTX 4090). If it can't be used, standard XeSS runs instead. Applies live.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.FastSuperResol: RTX 30 only, DirectX 12: faster DLSS Super Resolution for presets L and M. The image is very close to NVIDIA's but not identical. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.DLSSSRpreset.H: Game: no override. Applies to all quality modes; which presets work depends on the game's DLSS DLL. A to F are legacy. Applies live.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.DLSSRRpreset.H: Ray Reconstruction preset. Game: no override. A to C are legacy; D, E and F need nvngx_dlssd 310.9.1 or newer. Doesn't turn RR on. Applies live.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.SRHDRinput.Hel: Colour input mode for the upscaler. Game: follow the game. On: HDR linear input. Off: SDR input. Doesn't turn on display HDR. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.SRautoexposure: Upscaler auto exposure. Game: follow the game. Some DLSS presets (L) force it. XeSS auto exposure costs GPU time and isn't recommended for SDR. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.SmoothMotion.H: NVIDIA's driver frame interpolation, also for games without frame generation. RTX 30 (DirectX 11, 12, Vulkan) and experimental RTX 20 (DirectX 12, driver 621.01); RTX 40 and 50 get it from NVIDIA. Needs one of the drivers RTX Encore lists. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.GraphicsAPI.He: The game's graphics API, which Smooth Motion needs to know. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.NeuralRenderin: Turns DLSS Neural Rendering on. Needs the NR DLL above. The first launch prepares it in the background. Applies live.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.NRmodel.Label: NR model
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.NRmodel.Help: B (default): smaller and much faster. A: the larger network of NR 310.8.0. Auto: the DLL's choice (B). Applies live.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.NRprecision.He: RTX 20 and 30: Exact gives the same output as NVIDIA; Fast is quicker with small image differences. No effect on RTX 40 and 50. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.NRfastprocessi: Faster Neural Rendering processing with exactly the same output. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.GPUseries.Help: Leave on Auto unless RTX Encore detects your GPU wrongly. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.NVIDIAAppFGmod: Loads the frame generation models the NVIDIA App downloaded. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Disableingamem: For games that reject RTX Encore's in-game menu (Star Wars Outlaws). Frame generation keeps working; change settings here instead. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.FGinmenus.Help: Keeps frame generation running in menus and loading screens. Leave Off: idling at 1x there avoids device-hang crashes.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.RaytracedHairW: Prepares the ray-traced HairWorks conversion in games with a verified profile. The game's own hair setting still decides. Restart the game to apply.
Extras.RtxEncore.Settings.Intro: Set these before you play. Most need a game restart to apply (the tooltips say which). The overlay, Neural Rendering styles, shortcuts and diagnostics are in RTX Encore's in-game menu (Insert).

Extras.MfgAdaUnlock.Settings.Intro: MFG Ada Unlock unlocks DLSS multi frame generation (3x, 4x and 6x) on RTX 40 Series GPUs, or runs Intel XeSS frame generation (XeMFG, 2x to 6x) on RTX 20 to RTX 50 Series GPUs.
Extras.MfgAdaUnlock.Settings.VulkanWarni: This is a Vulkan game. As of MFG Ada Unlock 1.8.0, Vulkan support is experimental: Intel XeMFG (CUDA) needs the game to use DLSS Super Resolution or Ray Reconstruction, NVIDIA DLSS-G is experimental, and XeMFG via DLSS-G (XMX) is DirectX 12 only. Some Vulkan games also need a launch option before ReShade loads (for example +r_allowBlackListedLayers 1).
Extras.MfgAdaUnlock.Settings.ApiWarning: This game uses {0}. As of MFG Ada Unlock 1.8.0, it only works in DirectX 12 games (and experimentally in Vulkan games), so it won't work here.
Extras.MfgAdaUnlock.Settings.FgMethod.He: NVIDIA DLSS-G: NVIDIA's frame generation, 3x to 6x on RTX 40 Series (needs a DLSS Frame Generation DLL 310 or newer). Intel XeMFG (CUDA): Intel's XeSS frame generation, 2x to 6x on RTX 20 to RTX 50 Series. XeMFG via DLSS-G (XMX): the game's DLSS frame generation, with Intel's model generating the frames. Restart the game after changing this, and turn frame generation on in the game's own menu.
Extras.MfgAdaUnlock.Settings.Saved: Saved. Restart the game if it's running.
Extras.MfgAdaUnlock.Settings.DlssSr.Help: For games that use DLSS Super Resolution but have no DLSS frame generation for XeMFG to hook into. The camera is assumed and the HUD is interpolated with the scene. Only used with Intel XeMFG (CUDA). Restart the game after changing it.
Extras.MfgAdaUnlock.Settings.XessReady: Intel XeSS files (libxess_fg.dll and libxell.dll) are in the game folder, so both XeMFG methods are ready.
Extras.MfgAdaUnlock.Settings.XessWrongVe: The game folder has a version of Intel's XeSS files that MFG Ada Unlock doesn't accept ({0}). Reinstall MFG Ada Unlock to replace them. The game's own copies are kept as a backup and put back if you remove the mod.
Extras.MfgAdaUnlock.Settings.XessMissing: Intel XeSS files are missing from the game folder ({0}). Both XeMFG methods need them. Reinstall MFG Ada Unlock to add them.

Faq.Body.Extras:
The Extras section holds optional tools:
• Frame generation unlocks: Universal MFG Unlocker (RTX 40/30), MFG Ada Unlock (RTX 40), 20/30 FG Unlock (RTX 20/30), RTX Encore (beta) and DLSS Enabler.
• ASI Loader: loads .asi plugins.
• DXVK: runs DX8–DX11 games through Vulkan. The Lilium HDR variant gives older games HDR.
• dgVoodoo2: runs DX9 games through DX11.
Faq.Body.NeuralRendering:
The Neural Rendering section installs DLSS 5 neural rendering tools. RHI picks the right method for the game, and installs ReShade too if needed:
• ShortFuse DLSS Tool: most games with native DLSS.
• DLSS5 Tool: DX12 games with native DLSS.
• DLSS5 Tool + DX11 Bridge: DX11 and Vulkan games with native DLSS.
• DLSS5 Feeder: games without DLSS, including OpenGL, DX9 and 32-bit games.
Faq.Bullets.NvidiaDriverSettings.5: Multi Frame Generation (RTX 50): the Multi Frame Gen button in the DLSS / Streamline section
Faq.Bullets.Settings.6: Driver Settings: global NVIDIA driver defaults and profiles
Faq.Bullets.Settings.8: Tools & Maintenance: mass INI deploy, folders and logs, Full refresh and Purge staging files
Faq.Tip.Extras: Most of these ask which file name to use when you install them. Names already used by RHI's other components are disabled, and any game file that gets replaced is backed up.
Faq.Tip.NeuralRendering:
Each method's versions, and the NR DLL version, can be pinned or left on Latest.
NR Cost Scaler runs neural rendering at reduced cost. Turn it on before installing. ShortFuse already includes it.
Faq.Tip.WelcomeToRhi: Recommended first step: add a free GitHub token in Settings → Accounts & Data → GitHub token. Without one, GitHub allows only 60 requests an hour, which can make downloads and update checks fail. Create a classic token at github.com/settings/tokens with no boxes ticked, paste it in and click Save.

Settings.General.RunsRHIAdministratorWit: Runs RHI as administrator without a prompt each time. Needed for ReBAR, the DLSS indicator, Smooth Motion and Low Latency Ultra.
Settings.General.CreatesScheduledTaskLau: Creates a scheduled task that launches RHI with elevated privileges, so there is no prompt each time. Takes effect after RHI restarts.
Settings.General.OnlyUsedWhenAdminMode: Only used when Admin Mode is on.
Settings.Accounts.Title: Accounts & Data
Settings.Accounts.WhereRHIGetsItsMod: Where RHI gets its mod information, and the accounts it can use.
Settings.Accounts.TokenRaisesGitHubAPIRa: A token raises the GitHub API rate limit from 60 to 5,000 requests per hour. This improves reliability of update checks, DLSS version lookups, and manifest fetches.
Settings.Accounts.WithoutTokenRHILimited: Without a token RHI is limited to 60 GitHub requests an hour; a token raises it to 5,000.
Settings.Accounts.PasteGitHubPersonalAcc: Paste a GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT). It stays valid until you revoke it. No scopes needed, just generate and paste.
Settings.Accounts.OpensGithubComSettings: Opens github.com/settings/tokens. No boxes to tick: generate it and paste it above.
Settings.Accounts.RHIDatabaseUsesCommuni: RHI Database uses the community-maintained RHI database (recommended). RenoDX Wiki falls back to the RenoDX wiki scraper. Changing this setting triggers an immediate refresh.
Settings.Accounts.WhereRHILooksUpWhich: Where RHI looks up which games have mods. Changing it refreshes the library.
Settings.Accounts.ConnectSignsNexusModsB: Connect signs in to Nexus Mods in your browser. Premium users get one-click downloads and silent auto-updates. Free users get one-click browser downloads.
Settings.Accounts.SignNexusModsBrowserSo: Sign in to Nexus Mods in your browser so RHI can download mods from Nexus.
Settings.Accounts.SignOutNexusModsRemove: Sign out of Nexus Mods and remove the saved key.
Settings.Accounts.RegisterRHINxmHandlerS: Register RHI as the nxm:// handler so Nexus "Mod Manager Download" buttons open directly in RHI.
Settings.Accounts.OpenNexusModManagerDow: Open Nexus "Mod Manager Download" links in RHI.
Settings.ReShade.Title: ReShade & RenoDX
Settings.ReShade.DefaultsEveryGameUsingR: Defaults for every game using ReShade. Each game can still change these in its own ReShade ⚙.
Settings.ReShade.OpensReShadeOverlayGame: Opens the ReShade overlay in game. Click here and press a key to change it.
Settings.ReShade.WhereReShadeSavesScreen: Where ReShade saves screenshots. Type a folder and press Enter, or use Browse.
Settings.ReShade.WritesOverlayKeyScreens: Writes the overlay key, screenshot key, screenshot folder and effect list style into every game's reshade.ini. Skips hidden games and games set to keep their own reshade.ini.
Settings.ReShade.SkipsHiddenGamesGamesSe: Skips hidden games and games set to keep their own reshade.ini.
Settings.ReShade.MonitorSPeakBrightnessN: Your monitor's peak brightness in nits, written to reshade.ini presets. Press Enter to save.
Settings.ReShade.WritePeakBrightnessGame: Write peak brightness to all games
Settings.ReShade.WritesPeakNitsValueInto: Writes the peak nits value into every game's reshade.ini. Skips hidden games and games set to keep their own reshade.ini.
Settings.ReShade.RHIManagedDeployBuiltSh:
RHI Managed: deploy built-in shader packs to all games.
Custom: use your own shader directory.
Off: RHI never touches shaders on any game.
Settings.ReShade.ChangingUpdatesEveryGam: Changing this updates every game's shaders, so RHI asks first.
Settings.ReShade.PickFolderRHIWatchesAdd: Pick the folder RHI watches for addon downloads
Settings.ReShade.GoBackDownloadsFolder: Go back to your Downloads folder
Settings.ReShade.RHILooksHereRenoDXAddon: RHI looks here for RenoDX addon files you download.
Settings.Display.Title: Display & HDR
Settings.Display.WhatHappensScreenWhenLa: What happens to your screen when you launch a game through RHI, and display options without the NVIDIA Control Panel.
Settings.Display.UndoneAutomaticallyWhen: Undone automatically when the game closes.
Settings.Display.SelectWhichMonitorsChan: Select which monitors to change resolution on.
Settings.Display.BitsPerColourChannelSen: Bits per colour channel sent to the monitor. 10 bpc or higher suits HDR. Only depths your monitor and cable support will work.
Settings.Display.FullSuitsPCMonitorsLimi: Full suits PC monitors. Limited suits TVs that expect video levels. The wrong one makes blacks look grey or crushed.
Settings.Display.ApplyColourDepthDynamic: Apply the colour depth and dynamic range to the selected monitor.
Settings.Display.TurnDLDSRDeepLearningDy: Turn DLDSR (Deep Learning Dynamic Super Resolution) factors on or off without opening the NVIDIA Control Panel. Capture a state in the NVIDIA Control Panel first.
Settings.Display.AdjustDSRSmoothness0100: Adjust DSR smoothness (0-100%). Lower values are sharper, higher values are smoother. ~15 second display blackout on apply.
Settings.Display.ApplySelectedSmoothness: Apply the selected smoothness value. Causes ~15 second display blackout.
Settings.Display.SelectPreviouslyCapture: Select a previously captured DLDSR state to apply.
Settings.Display.ApplySelectedDLDSRState: Apply the selected DLDSR state. Causes ~15 second display blackout.
Settings.Display.ScreenGoesBlackAbout15: The screen goes black for about 15 seconds when you set smoothness or apply a state.
Settings.Display.CaptureCurrentDLDSRStat: Capture the current DLDSR state from NVIDIA Control Panel. Configure DLDSR in NVIDIA CP first, then capture.
Settings.Display.DeleteCurrentlySelected: Delete the currently selected saved state.
Settings.Display.RefreshCurrentDLDSRStat: Refresh the current DLDSR state from registry.
Settings.Dlss.Title: DLSS / Streamline
Settings.Dlss.MatchesDLSSStreamlineSecti: Matches the DLSS / Streamline section in each game's panel.
Settings.Dlss.VersionsPresetsRenderScale: Versions, presets and render scales that Quick Apply (in each game's DLSS / Streamline section) puts on a game.
Settings.Dlss.ChooseDLSSStreamlineVersio: Choose the DLSS / Streamline versions, presets and render scales that Quick Apply uses.
Settings.Dlss.AutomaticDLSSStreamlineUpd: Automatic DLSS and Streamline updates: General › Updates.
Settings.Dlss.IndicatorFrameGenerationBa: Indicator, frame generation and batch deploy
Settings.Dlss.NeedsAdminModeGeneralWindo: Needs Admin Mode (General › Windows and Admin Mode).
Settings.Dlss.GlobalDynamicMultiFrameGen: Global Dynamic Multi Frame Generation (DMFG) defaults. Set these once, then just enable Dynamic mode in each game's MFG dialog.
Settings.Dlss.PutDLSSStreamlineVersionsP: Put DLSS and Streamline versions and presets on many games at once.
Settings.Driver.Title: Driver Settings
Settings.Driver.DriverDefaultsEveryGameG: Driver defaults for every game. A game's own Driver Settings section overrides these.
Settings.Driver.DriverLevelSettingsAppli: Driver-level settings applied globally via the base NVIDIA profile. Per-game settings are in the Driver Settings section of each game's panel.
Settings.Driver.GlobalFPSCapViaNVIDIA: Global FPS cap via NVIDIA driver. VRR-optimal presets cap just below refresh rate to stay in VRR range. Choosing a cap also turns the per-game FPS limit Off for every game with ReLimiter or Display Commander, so the two limiters don't fight.
Settings.Driver.ShowsNVIDIASGSync: Shows NVIDIA's G-Sync indicator in games when G-Sync is active. Global driver setting, affects all games.
Settings.Driver.CreatesNVIDIADriverProfi: Creates NVIDIA driver profiles for all games that don't have one yet. Games without a profile don't get the driver defaults above (Power Mode, VSync and so on).
Settings.Driver.SavePerGameNVIDIAProfile: Save all per-game NVIDIA profile settings to a backup file. Useful before updating drivers.
Settings.Driver.RestorePerGameNVIDIAProf: Restore per-game NVIDIA profile settings from a previous backup.
Settings.Driver.TheseCanTUndoneEach: These can't be undone. Each asks first, with Cancel as the default.
Settings.Components.Title: Components
Settings.Components.DefaultsReLimiterOpt: Defaults for ReLimiter and OptiScaler. Each game's ⚙ overrides these.
Settings.Components.WritesOverlayKeyShar: Writes the overlay key, Shared presets, DLSS hooks and Target FPS into every game's relimiter.ini. Skips hidden games.
Settings.Components.GPUBrandPCRHIUses: The GPU brand in this PC. RHI uses it to pick which OptiScaler.ini to install. DLSS inputs appears for AMD and Intel.
Settings.Components.OptiScalerReportsNVI: On: OptiScaler reports an NVIDIA GPU to the game, so the game offers DLSS and OptiScaler uses its inputs. Off: no GPU spoofing. Used when OptiScaler.ini is installed.
Settings.Components.KeyOpensOptiScalerOv: The key that opens the OptiScaler overlay in game. Saved straight away for new installs; use the button to update games that already have OptiScaler.
Settings.Components.WriteKeyOptiScalerGa: Write key to all OptiScaler games
Settings.Components.WritesOverlayKeyInto: Writes the overlay key into OptiScaler.ini in every game that has OptiScaler installed. Skips hidden games.
Settings.Tools.Title: Tools & Maintenance
Settings.Tools.BulkActionsFoldersLogsLas: Bulk actions, folders and logs, and last-resort fixes.
Settings.Tools.DeployINIFilesReShadePres: Deploy INI files or ReShade presets to many games at once. Your hotkeys and screenshot folder are kept.
Settings.Tools.InstallReShadePresetIntoM: Install a ReShade preset into many games at once.
Settings.Tools.RHIDataStoredAppDataLogs: All RHI data is stored in AppData. The Logs folder contains session usage logs useful for troubleshooting.
Settings.Tools.DropOwnReShadeDLSSStreaml: Drop your own ReShade, DLSS or Streamline DLLs into the Custom folder to use them as per-game overrides.
Settings.Tools.OpenRHISDataFolder: Open RHI's data folder in AppData
Settings.Tools.OpenCustomFolderOwnReShad: Open the Custom folder for your own ReShade, DLSS or Streamline DLLs
Settings.Tools.UseTheseIfSomethingBadly: Use these if something is badly wrong. Each asks first.
